name: Jumada al-Awwal
intro:
In this month, only the days 5, 6, 10, 13, 15, 25, 27 and 29 coincide with important events of history.
The birth of Lady Zaynab (PBUH) is the good news of this month. The Battle of Mu'tah and the Battle of the Camel are two major events of this month.
The martyrdom of Lady Zahra (PBUH) and the handing over of Imam Husayn's (PBUH) shirt to Lady Zaynab (PBUH) are two heart-rending events of this month. The passing of 'Abd al-Muttalib (PBUH) and the passing of Muhammad ibn 'Uthman al-'Amri are also among the events of this month, and the death of Mu'awiya, son of Yazid, brought the rule of the Umayyads to an end.

events.title: Birth of Lady Zaynab (PBUH)
events.text:
The blessed birth of Lady Zaynab (PBUH) took place on this day in Medina, in the 5th or 6th year after the Hijra. Other accounts of her birth are: 5 Jumada al-Awwal 6 AH, early Sha'ban 6 AH, the month of Ramadan 6 AH, and the last ten days of Rabi' al-Thani in the year 5, 6 or 7 AH.
Her noble father is Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and her honored mother is Lady Siddiqa Tahira (PBUH). Her husband was 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), and her children were 'Ali, 'Awn, 'Abbas, Muhammad and Umm Kulthum, of whom 'Awn and Muhammad were martyred at Karbala.
Her kunyas (honorific by-names) are Umm Kulthum, Umm 'Abd Allah and Umm al-Hasan, but her special kunyas are Umm al-Masa'ib (Mother of Calamities), Umm al-Raza'a and Umm al-Naw'a'ib.
Her titles are many, among them: 'Aqilat Bani Hashim, 'Aqilat al-Talibiyyin, Sadaqa Sughra (an allusion to her mother, who is Siddiqa Kubra, and her father, who is Siddiq Akbar), 'Ismat Sughra, Waliyyat Allah, al-Radiya bi'l-Qadar wa'l-Qada', Sabirat al-Bala' min ghayri jaza' wa la shakwa, Aminat Allah, 'Alima ghayr Mu'allama, Fahima ghayr Mufahhama, Mahbubat al-Mustafa (SAWW), Thaniyat al-Zahra (PBUH), and al-Sharifa.
Many children were born from the lineage of 'Ali, the son of Lady Zaynab (PBUH), who are known as the Zaynabis; al-Suyuti composed a treatise on them called Risalat al-Zaynabiyya.
sources: 'Aqilat Bani Hashim (PBUH): p. 5. Zaynab al-Kubra (PBUH): p. 17. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 94-95. Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, p. 33.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 113. Tarikh al-Khamis: vol. 2, p. 317. Tadhkirat al-Khawass: p. 4.

subsections.title: The Story of Her Birth
subsections.text:
At the time of her birth, the Prophet (SAWW) was away on a journey. Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), regarding the naming of this newborn, said: “I will not precede the Prophet (SAWW).” Then the Prophet came and awaited revelation. Jibra'il descended and said: “God sends His greetings and says: ‘Name this girl Zaynab, for We have written this name on the Preserved Tablet.’”
The Prophet (SAWW) called for Lady Zaynab (PBUH), kissed her, and said: “I entrust those present and those absent to honor this girl for my sake, for she is indeed like Khadija al-Kubra (PBUH).” Her serenity and dignity have been likened to Khadija al-Kubra (PBUH), her chastity and modesty to Fatima Zahra (PBUH), her eloquence and rhetoric to 'Ali al-Murtada (PBUH), her forbearance and patience to Hasan al-Mujtaba (PBUH), and her courage and strength of heart to Sayyid al-Shuhada' (PBUH).
Ibn Hajar in al-Isaba and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghaba wrote about her circumstances: in the assembly of Yazid, may God's curse be upon him, Lady Zaynab (PBUH) spoke words that indicate her strength of heart. She was renowned among the House of Bani Hashim and the Arabs for her generosity, insight and forbearance, and she combined beauty and majesty, character and appearance, morality and virtue. She spent her nights in worship and her days fasting, and she was known among the God-fearing.
sources: Majallat al-Islam: issue 27, Muhammad Ghalib al-Shafi'i.

events.title: Battle of Mu'tah
events.text:
On such a day in the 7th year of the Hijra, the Battle of Mu'tah took place. The number of Muslims in this battle was three thousand, and the number of disbelievers was one hundred thousand.
This war began when Harith ibn 'Umayr al-Azdi, who was carrying a letter from the Prophet (SAWW) to Caesar of Rome, was arrested in the lands of Mu'tah on the order of Shurahbil ibn 'Amr, a commander of the Roman army; his hands were bound and he was beheaded. The Prophet (SAWW) was deeply grieved upon hearing this news and sent an army to Mu'tah.
In this battle, the Prophet (SAWW) and Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) were not present, and the Prophet appointed three commanders in succession over the army, saying: “If one is martyred, let the next be commander of the army: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Haritha, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha.”

subsections.title: The Martyrdom of the Three Commanders
subsections.text:
All three of these noble men were martyred. First Ja'far came to the battlefield, and after valiant combat both of his hands were cut off. Even though many wounds had been inflicted on Ja'far's body, because of his awe and courage on the battlefield no one dared to sever his head. Therefore the enemy attacked all at once and lifted his body from the ground with spears. At that very moment the Prophet (SAWW) was on the pulpit in Medina, recounting the events to the people. Suddenly he raised his blessed face toward the sky and prayed for Ja'far. God granted him two wings, with which he flies with the angels in Paradise.
After the martyrdom of all three commanders appointed by the Prophet (SAWW), they were buried in a single grave. Upon hearing the news of Ja'far's martyrdom, the Prophet (SAWW) wept profusely and ordered that food be taken to Ja'far's house for three days.

subsections.title: Ja'far's Background
subsections.text:
The first man after 'Ali (PBUH) who, by the order of Abu Talib (PBUH), prayed behind the Prophet (SAWW) was Ja'far. He was ten years older than his brother Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).
In Abyssinia, when 'Amr ibn al-'As and others intended to persuade the Negus to hand over Ja'far and his companions, he recited verses of the Divine Book, and the Negus and those around him wept. 'Amr ibn al-'As tried several times to portray Ja'far and the Muslims as dishonest before the Negus, but the result was the opposite and their esteem rose in the eyes of the Negus, especially when verses concerning Jesus (PBUH) were recited.
Finally, 'Amr ibn al-'As prepared poisoned food and sent it to Ja'far in order to martyr him, but a cat came and ate a little of that food and spilled the rest, and the cat died, and 'Amr ibn al-'As's plot was exposed.
On the day of the conquest of Khaybar, Ja'far, together with his wife and the other Muslims, came to Medina, and the Prophet (SAWW) was very happy at their arrival and said: “I do not know which makes me happier: the conquest of Khaybar or the arrival of Ja'far!”
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 57-58. Siri dar Sharh-e Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 2, pp. 410-414. Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 94.

events.title: Battle of the Camel (Jamal)
events.text:
On such a day in the year 36 AH, the Battle of the Camel took place, Basra was conquered, and God's gracious victory descended upon Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). Kaf'ami (RA) considers the 15th of this month to be the day of the Battle of the Camel.
The beginning of this event was that after the people pledged allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), Talha and Zubayr left Medina under the pretext of performing 'Umra and joined 'A'isha. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, who had previously been 'Uthman's governor in Basra and had been dismissed by Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), came to Mecca and brought 'A'isha a camel he had bought for two hundred dinars, and they set out toward Basra until they reached the city. After entering, they stormed the house of 'Uthman ibn Hunayf, the governor appointed by Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), took him captive and beat him severely.
Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) set out toward Basra to confront them. In this battle, accompanying Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) were Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUH), as well as Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, the sons of 'Aqil, a number of the youth of Bani Hashim, together with 'Ammar, Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and a number of the Muhajirun and Ansar. Eighty of the companions of Badr, 250 of those who had taken part in the Pledge of the Tree (Bay'at al-Shajara) with the Prophet (SAWW), and 1,500 of the other companions of the Prophet (SAWW) took part.
He sent Muslim al-Mujashi'i with a Qur'an to call the Basrans to the judgment of the Qur'an, but they made Muslim a target of their arrows and martyred him. After the admonitions of 'Ammar and the words of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), on the tenth of Jumada al-Awwal they continued the war that 'A'isha had started, and Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) set out to confront them. In this war, of the army of Amir al-Mu'minin, which numbered 20,000 fighters, five thousand were martyred, and of 'A'isha's army, which numbered 30,000, 13,000 were killed.
Finally, when victory went to the army of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), he came to 'A'isha's howdah and said: “O Humayra', did the Prophet command you to come out to fight me? Did he not command you to sit in your house and not come out? By God, those who kept their own women hidden behind the curtain and brought you out did not act justly.” Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr pulled his sister out of the howdah. Amir al-Mu'minin ordered that she be taken to the house of Safiyya, daughter of Harith ibn Abi Talha, and afterwards sent her to Mecca, and from Mecca to Medina. In this battle Zayd ibn Sawhan, who was one of the leading figures of the army and one of the Shi'a of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), was martyred, and the Imam came to his side and said: “O Zayd, may God have mercy on you, for your worldly attachments were few and your support for the faith was great.”
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 17-22. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 239.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 31. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 384. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 597. al-'Udda al-Qawiyya: p. 53. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 733.

Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 32, pp. 174, 196, 211. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 159-161. The number of martyrs of the army of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) has been given as one thousand and seventy, and also one thousand seven hundred; by one account, even four.

events.title: Handing over the Shirt of Imam Husayn (PBUH) to Lady Zaynab (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day Lady Zahra (PBUH) gave the shirt of Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman (PBUH) to Zaynab al-Kubra (PBUH) and said: “When your brother Husayn (PBUH) asks you for this shirt, know that he will be your guest for no more than an hour, and then he will be killed in the worst of states at the hands of the bastards.”
This event took place three days before the martyrdom of Lady Zahra (PBUH).

events.title: Martyrdom of Lady Zahra (PBUH)
events.text:
The oppressed and heart-rending martyrdom of Hadrat Imam al-A'imma al-Nujaba' (leader of the noble Imams), Siddiqa Kubra Fatima Zahra (PBUH) took place in Medina 75 days after the passing of the Prophet (SAWW). Other accounts regarding the martyrdom of the Lady will be given under the 3rd of Jumada al-Thaniya.
On the night of the fourteenth, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), together with a small group of the choicest of his companions, laid the pure body of Siddiqa Kubra (PBUH) to rest.
It has been narrated with a sound chain of transmission from Imam Sadiq (PBUH) that Lady Fatima (PBUH) lived for 75 days after the Prophet (SAWW). According to the well-known view that the Prophet's passing was on 28 Safar, the martyrdom of Lady Siddiqa (PBUH) falls on 13, 14 or 15 Jumada al-Awwal; visiting her shrine is recommended on these three days.
sources: Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 374. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 246. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 545.

events.title: Passing of 'Abd al-Muttalib (PBUH)
events.text: In the eighth year after the birth of the Prophet (SAWW), 'Abd al-Muttalib passed away. It should be noted that, according to 'Allama Majlisi in Mir'at al-'Uqul, 8 years, 2 months and 10 days of the blessed age of the Messenger of God (SAWW) had passed when 'Abd al-Muttalib (PBUH) died; if it is a lunar year, the day of his passing is 27 Jumada al-Awwal, and if a solar year is meant, it comes to approximately 27 Sha'ban. Another account of his passing is the tenth of Rabi' al-Awwal.
sources: Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 5. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 5. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Awwal volume, p. 67.

events.title: Passing of Muhammad ibn 'Uthman al-'Amri
events.text: The passing of the second special deputy of the Imam of the Age (may God's blessings be upon him), Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-'Amri (RA), took place on such a day.
sources: Ghayba of Shaykh Tusi: p. 364. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Sha'ban volume, p. 345. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 231

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
